title: Verified uniform candidate families and knapsack rounding for nested-logit assortments
description:
This technical note and reproducible Lean packet complete the uniform quadratic candidate-family theorem used by Guillermo Gallego and Huseyin Topaloglu in Constrained Assortment Optimization for the Nested Logit Model (Management Science, DOI 10.1287/mnsc.2014.1931). For the exact finite nested-logit knapsack interface, one feasible family of at most (n+1)^2 assortments gives a factor-two utility approximation simultaneously for every nonnegative parameter u. The archive also contains the accepted fractional-knapsack optimizer construction, the factor-two rounding inequality and the separate 1/(1-epsilon) small-item bound.

The new proof partitions nonnegative parameters by strict and weak comparisons with crossings of the n utility/space ratio lines and the zero line. Ties, crossing points, parallel lines and coincident lines are included. A reconstructed nonnegative dual multiplier transports an actual optimal primal LP point within each cell. Rounded representatives and all feasible singletons yield the stated cardinality; the empty assortment is already a representative. The full multi-nest revenue algorithm, a running-time theorem and a refined uniform small-item guarantee remain separate.

Four exact Prove2Me-accepted source files are retained byte-for-byte, with complete independent target audits, all three required platform definitions, immutable Lean 4.33.1/Mathlib dependency pins, the established archive verifier and fresh reproduction logs. The checks use autoImplicit=false and allow only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Deliberately invalid controls reject an unused local axiom, a weaker substitute for the entire new Theorem6, and a changed proof byte. Third-party compiled caches remain trusted inputs; no compiler bootstrap verification is claimed.

The source mathematics belongs to Gallego and Topaloglu; the shared instance also credits James M. Davis. The platform cites September 11, 2013; the inspected author-hosted revision is September 18, 2013, and no original-PDF hash or version identity is asserted. mikedeng1 supplied the platform statements and definitions; Shuze Chen reviewed statements. Earlier accepted queelius proofs and Lean/Mathlib infrastructure retain specific credit. Alexander Richard Towell directed the work; substantial OpenAI Codex proof development, verification and documentation assistance is disclosed. No mathematical novelty, source-author endorsement or independent human proof review is claimed.

Version 1.2.0 is a substantive successor in the existing archive family. The new complete Theorem6 was publicly submitted and accepted on October 21, 2026; the original three proofs were submitted on October 20. These disclosure and acceptance timestamps are recorded separately from archival publication. Version 1.1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23526994, remains the exact three-proof edition. The owning development repository stays private; the central research-records entry supplies curated public links.
notes: Four accepted target IDs and exact hashes are included. Theorem6 reuses the earlier accepted optimizer and rounding bodies without counting them as new targets. Original authors and prior contributors are credited as predecessors, not represented as coauthors of this note. Earlier metadata retains its MIT grant; exact public platform sources and archival edition use Apache-2.0.
